expected_evidence: Geological: platinum-group element (Pt/Ir) anomaly, magnetic microspherules, nanodiamonds, and a 'black mat' organic-rich layer dated to ~10,950 BCE across North American stratigraphic sections (the 'Younger Dryas Boundary' layer)
Geological/ice-core: synchronous platinum spike in Greenland ice cores at the YD onset
Material/archaeological: abrupt discontinuity or decline in Clovis-culture artifact density and site occupation immediately above the YDB layer; abrupt megafaunal extinction horizon
Material: soot/charcoal layers indicating continent-scale biomass burning at the same horizon
Astronomical: physical impact crater or airburst structure of appropriate age (none confirmed to date) and/or tektite/impactite fields
Genetic: population bottleneck signature in ancient/modern Native American mtDNA or Y-chromosome lineages coinciding with ~10,950 BCE; parallel bottleneck signal in surviving megafauna genomes
Oral tradition/iconographic: indigenous flood-fire-sky-event narratives speculatively linked to the event (very weak, low-confidence category)
response.rationale: The hypothesis matches the well-known Younger Dryas Impact Hypothesis (YDIH), interval -10950 corresponding to the YD onset (~12,900 cal BP). The period field was left unspecified in the hypothesis, but the date places it at the Younger Dryas boundary, so I applied the 'younger-dryas' row rather than a generic prior (model-prior, low confidence, since the period label itself was not given). Geological (0.65) and astronomical/ice-core (0.7) detectability are comparatively high for this period — and indeed this is exactly the category of evidence (Pt/Ir anomalies, nanodiamonds, black mats, ice-core platinum spikes) that has been reported in the literature, so absence of any geological trace would be surprising if the hypothesis were true. However, the hypothesis specifically claims an effect on 'population-demography,' which requires material (0.35) and genetic (0.3) evidence — lines with much lower survivability in this era, and no confirmed impact crater or definitive demographic-collapse signal has been established; the causal chain from ejecta fallout to population decline remains actively disputed in the literature (contested by many geologists who attribute Pt/microspherule signals to non-impact processes, and by archaeologists who dispute a Clovis population collapse). Textual (0.0) and linguistic (0.05) evidence are essentially non-existent by definition (pre-literate), and oral tradition (0.1)/iconographic (0.1) evidence, while sometimes invoked, is low-reliability and highly speculative for dating this precisely. Given the mix — real, searchable geological/astronomical proxies exist and have been reported, but the specific demographic-causation claim rests on the weaker material/genetic evidence lines — a low-to-moderate detectability adjustment (~0.4) is appropriate: absence of a confirmed demographic-collapse signal or impact crater should not be treated as strong evidence of falsity, since detectability for the demographic-specific claim is intrinsically low, even though some contested geological evidence has genuinely been found and debated in the mainstream literature (per model-prior, unverified beyond general familiarity with the YDIH debate).
